title: Birch and Bramble's Big Walk
markdown:
In the Starberry Hills, high above the gentle rolling hills where the whisper-grass grew, lived a little elf named Birch. His home was a wonderfully cosy nook, nestled amongst soft green mosses that felt like a velvet blanket, and here he always felt safe and so very warm. Birch had a very special friend, a little hedgehog named Bramble. Bramble was a perfectly round and soft little creature, with tiny happy prickles that would give the gentlest tickle when he wiggled with happiness. He loved Birch more than anything.

One lovely morning, the sunbeams spilled like warm golden honey through Birch’s little window, and a soft sweet breeze whispered secrets to the tall quiet pine trees outside. Birch held a tiny beautifully wrapped parcel in his hands. The paper was the colour of a pale blue sky, tied with a ribbon the shade of a ripe strawberry. “Bramble, my dearest little friend,” Birch whispered, his voice as soft and light as a dandelion seed floating on the air, “this parcel needs to go to Mrs Meadowsweet, who lives in the little cottage just beyond the softly echoing pine wood. Would you, oh would you, help me deliver it?” Bramble gave a happy little sniffle and wiggled his nose, a wiggle so full of joy and eagerness that it was his special way of saying yes please.

So, with the sunbeams guiding their way, Birch and Bramble set off on their little adventure. The pine wood was alive with the gentlest of sounds. The wind rustled the tall ancient trees, making them sway and dance like sleepy graceful dancers. Little dappled shadows, playing a quiet game of hide-and-seek, danced on the mossy winding path below. The air itself smelled wonderfully sweet, like warm pine needles mixed with the fresh damp earth after a morning dew. Birch hummed a quiet happy tune, a little melody that seemed to float on the breeze, and Bramble trotted along beside him, his little feet making soft gentle pattering sounds on the forest floor. It was a peaceful lovely walk.

As they ambled along, their happy little journey meandering through the trees, they heard a most delightful sweet smell wafting towards them on the gentle breeze. Oh, it was the warm yummy smell of freshly baked cakes. Peeking around a big mossy rock, smooth and cool to the touch, they saw a small cheerful goblin with a rosy nose, carefully tending to a little wooden cart. The cart was piled high with the most yummy-looking golden-brown treats. “Hello there, little ones,” the goblin chirped, his voice like the tinkling of tiny cheerful bells. “Would you like a starberry swirl or a honey-dew drop? They’re fresh from the oven, warm and wonderful.” Birch smiled a wide happy smile that reached his eyes. “Oh, how lovely,” he said, his voice full of delight. “We’re on our way to deliver a parcel to Mrs Meadowsweet, but a little treat would be absolutely wonderful.” Bramble, who always, always loved a tasty nibble, gave a happy little squeak of agreement. The goblin, with a kindly wink, carefully placed a tiny warm honey-dew drop on a little smooth leaf for Bramble and a delicate swirly starberry sweet for Birch. They were indeed very yummy, a perfect little burst of sweetness that made their tummies feel warm and content, like a cosy hug from the inside.

After thanking the kind goblin with many cheerful smiles, Birch and Bramble continued on their way, their spirits lifted by the sweet treat. They listened closely to the ever-changing sounds of the wood, and soon they heard a most funny, yet not at all scary, sound. It wasn’t loud or startling, not even a little bit. It was a deep rumbling Huuuummm-snuffle-snore, a sound that seemed to come from very far away, yet also very near. They tiptoed closer, their movements as light as falling leaves, and through a parting in the trees, they saw a big sleepy dragon. He was curled up in a patch of warm golden sunbeam, fast asleep and dreaming happy dreams. His scales shimmered with soft warm colours, like a beautiful sunset painted across the sky, and his snores sounded like a gentle rocking lullaby, a peaceful rhythm that made the air feel calm. Birch whispered, his voice barely a breath, “Oh, he’s just having a very long peaceful nap. We must be very quiet so as not to disturb his sleep.” Bramble nodded solemnly, his little nose twitching with quiet understanding. The dragon’s snores were so peaceful and steady, they almost made Birch feel a little sleepy too.

Just a little way beyond the sleeping dragon, Birch’s sharp eyes spied a tiny brightly painted cottage with a thin wisp of smoke curling softly from its chimney, like a gentle breath of steam. “We’re here, Bramble,” Birch whispered excitedly, his heart giving a little happy bounce. They walked up to the little wooden door, painted a cheerful robin’s egg blue, and gently tapped. The door opened with a soft creak, and a kind face with twinkling warm eyes looked down at them. It was Mrs Meadowsweet. “Oh, hello Birch and Bramble,” she said warmly, her voice like a gentle melody. “And what a lovely parcel you have brought me.” Birch proudly, with a flutter of joy, handed her the little gift. Mrs Meadowsweet smiled a big beaming smile. “Thank you both so very much. You are such kind wonderful helpers.”

Birch and Bramble felt a lovely warm feeling spread through them. They had helped, and they had been brave enough to explore a little, seeing new and wonderful things. They waved goodbye to Mrs Meadowsweet, who waved back with a smile, and turned back towards home. The pine wood felt even more friendly and familiar now, as the sky above began to turn to soft dreamy shades of purple and pink, the colours of twilight. The sleepy dragon was still snoozing peacefully, his snores a gentle rumble, and the sounds of the wood were just gentle whispers of the coming night. Birch held Bramble close as they walked, feeling very happy and very safe.

Soon they were back in their cosy nook, their own special haven. The moon, a sliver of pale light, was just peeking over the Starberry Hills, casting a soft silvery glow that made everything look a little bit like magic. Birch snuggled into his warm soft bed, pulling his mossy blanket up to his chin, and Bramble curled up in his own little mossy nest right beside him, a small contented ball of fluff. The day had been a lovely adventure, full of yummy treats, friendly faces, and gentle discoveries. Birch closed his eyes, feeling the gentle slow rhythm of his own breathing, and listened to the soft peaceful sounds of the night outside. The parcel was delivered. The dragon still snored. Bramble’s prickles still tickled, which was how you knew a honey-dew drop could pause a walk and still get a ribbon to Mrs Meadowsweet.
characters: Birch (little elf of the Starberry Hills), Bramble (a round soft hedgehog)
